plays.name: Google Forms comparison + Search test
plays.oneLiner: Use Formkit’s existing Google Forms comparison as one focused page, then test it with capped Search Ads.

plays.trigger: A buyer searches for a Google Forms alternative because they need branded links or question-level drop-off insights.
plays.hook: Using Google Forms but need a branded link and question-level drop-off? Compare the differences and try Formkit’s free plan. https://formkit.app/
plays.mechanic: Use one focused comparison page as the landing page for high-intent Search Ads. Keep the comparison fair and send visitors to the free plan.
plays.assetUsed: Formkit’s existing Google Forms comparison at https://formkit.app/; focus it on branded links, question-level drop-off, and partial responses.
funnel: 90-day scenario: $1,800 total ad spend, assuming the $600 monthly budget continues for three months after test gates; CPC $3 / $2 / $1, assumption, grade D, yields 600 / 900 / 1,800 clicks. The initial $600 test alone yields about 200 / 300 / 600 clicks at those assumed CPCs.

Click → free sign-up: 1% / 3% / 5%, assumption, grade D. The comparison-page catalog cites 8.43% average conversion across 95 articles, vendor-sourced, grade C; this forecast uses lower planning rates: https://www.eesel.ai/blog/how-to-create-comparison-and-alternative-pages.
Free sign-up → paying customer: 1% / 3% / 5%, assumption, grade D; Formkit conversion data was not supplied. Likely path: 900 clicks × 3% × 3% = 0.81 paying customers.
plays.unit: paying customers in 90 days, assuming the full conditional ad budget is used.
plays.biggestUnknown: Search CPC and visitor-to-paid conversion; neither is known for Formkit.
plays.test: Run Google Search Ads for 30 days, capped at $600. Target 300 clicks at the assumed $2 CPC; stop at budget or day 30. At day 21, review results after roughly 200 clicks.
plays.killIf: Pause if 100 clicks produce no free sign-ups. Do not continue beyond the $600 test without a paid customer and an all-in CAC within the confirmed ceiling.
plays.scaleIf: At day 21, continue through day 30 if at least 6 of roughly 200 clicks become free sign-ups. After day 30, continue at no more than $600/month only if at least one customer has paid and all-in CAC is at or below 50% of confirmed 12-month gross profit per account. This 50% ceiling is a policy assumption; no additional budget is authorized until the dollar ceiling is known.
plays.firstActionToday: Ask ClimbOS to draft a focused page from the existing comparison and a matching Search ad; review both before publishing.
plays.climbosCanDo: ClimbOS drafts the focused page and ad, sets up tracked links, and reports sign-ups and paid customers. The owner approves and launches the ad.

plays.name: Studio intake outreach
plays.oneLiner: Use personalized outreach to studios that manage client intake across projects.
plays.audience: Independent web and design studios found through Clutch and studio websites. Clutch is a relevant directory, but the size of the reachable audience was not established: https://clutch.co/.
plays.trigger: A studio takes on a client and needs a repeatable intake process.
plays.hook: Build a client-intake form once, reuse shared templates, and manage client workspaces in one place. https://formkit.app/use-cases/agencies.
plays.mechanic: ClimbOS finds relevant studios, uses published business emails, writes a personal first line, sends from the owner’s mailbox, follows up, and stops on reply. The pitch is a reusable client-intake workflow, not a generic form-builder pitch.
plays.assetUsed: Formkit’s agency use case, including client workspaces and shared templates: https://formkit.app/use-cases/agencies.
funnel: Target 3,000 sends over 90 days: 250 contacts/week for 12 weeks, an operational assumption. ClimbOS’s stated capacity is 600–1,000 emails/month per mailbox after warm-up; the number of matching, reachable studios is unverified.

Sent → reply: 1% / 2.5% / 3%. ClimbOS’s operating range is 1–3% in the brief; the 2025 B2B average is 3.43%, vendor aggregate, grade B: https://instantly.ai. The 2.5% planning rate is an assumption, grade D.
Reply → booked call: 20% / 30% / 40%, ClimbOS operating benchmark in the brief, grade B.
Booked call → paying customer: 10% / 20% / 30%, assumption, grade D; Formkit close-rate data was not supplied. Likely path: 3,000 sends × 2.5% × 30% × 20% = 4.5 paying customers.
plays.unit: paying customers in 90 days, assuming the planned 3,000 contacts are reached.
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether replies turn into paid accounts, and whether enough suitable studios can be reached.
plays.test: ClimbOS researches and contacts 500 published business emails over 21 days. No ad spend; include actual ClimbOS credit charges and owner call time in CAC. Value owner time at $50/hour as the playbook’s cost assumption.
plays.killIf: After 500 sends, stop or change the audience if fewer than 5 reply. If 5–12 reply, revise the audience or hook before expanding; do not exceed the test volume.
plays.scaleIf: At day 21, if at least 13 of 500 contacts reply and at least 4 calls are booked, continue at 250 contacts per week through day 90. That is about 1,000 contacts per month; at the likely funnel rates, the remaining contacts imply roughly 3.7 additional paying customers. Stop expansion if all-in CAC exceeds 50% of confirmed 12-month gross profit per account; that ceiling is a policy assumption.
plays.firstActionToday: Approve a Clutch and studio-website prospect profile for ClimbOS to use in the first contact list.
plays.climbosCanDo: ClimbOS researches prospects, finds published business emails, writes personalized openers, sends and follows up, and tracks replies in the Pipeline. The owner handles calls and closing.

plays.name: Finish the workflow
plays.oneLiner: Measure the closest route to payment before buying more visits; this is not yet a bankable recommendation.
plays.audience: Existing free Formkit workspaces with recent paid-feature intent and permission to receive relevant product emails; exclude users acquired by the other plays from this forecast.
plays.trigger: A recorded attempt to use a paid feature, such as a custom domain or payments.
plays.hook: Need your own domain or Stripe payments? Formkit Pro is $6 per seat per month. Payments go to your own Stripe account, and Formkit takes no cut. Open your workspace: https://formkit.app.
plays.mechanic: Send one workflow-specific email after the actual attempt, with one reminder maximum and a tested return link. Hypothesis: resolving an immediate paid-feature need converts better than a general upgrade announcement.
plays.assetUsed: Formkit’s own feature-attempt data and the direct path from a free workspace to its relevant paid workflow.
funnel: Eligible existing free workspaces → delivered trigger email: 95% / 98% / 100%; assumption, grade D. Forecast input: 500 delivered emails, subject to cohort availability.

Delivered email → click: 1% / 2% / 3%; assumption, grade D, informed by the supplied 2.09% email-campaign click benchmark [https://www.mailerlite.com/, grade A]; that aggregate does not establish Formkit’s upgrade rate.
Click → resume the attempted workflow: 50% / 75% / 90%; assumption, grade D.
Resumed workflow → first payment: 10% / 30% / 40%; assumption, grade D.
plays.biggestUnknown: The size and historical upgrade rate of the eligible cohort; these must establish whether this can become the bankable play.
plays.test: Assumed test: 500 eligible existing free workspaces, $60 total cost including owner time and credits; clicks checked on day 21, payments on day 45. If fewer qualify, use the actual count and reduce the forecast proportionally.
plays.killIf: Four or fewer clicks from 500 delivered emails, or no payments by day 45. Change the hook once; stop if the result repeats.
plays.scaleIf: At least 10 clicks and three first payments from 500 delivered emails, with actual CAC below half the verified 12-month gross profit. Then cover every eligible attempt weekly; the planning volume is about 40 workspaces a week.
plays.firstActionToday: Spend 20 minutes exporting recent paid-feature attempts and checking whether the corresponding workspaces are reachable.
plays.climbosCanDo: Build the trigger and return link, process every eligible attempt weekly, and track delivery, clicks, resumed workflows and first payments.

plays.name: Chat-built intake, team-approved
plays.oneLiner: Sell the team approval step after AI builds the client-intake form.
plays.audience: US agencies with 2–10 people and visible client-intake work; research through https://clutch.co and agency websites, using only published business emails.
plays.trigger: An agency reviewing its next client-onboarding process; January planning is a timing hypothesis, not verified seasonal demand.
plays.hook: Does someone approve your client-intake forms before they go live? Formkit lets you build and publish forms from Claude or ChatGPT, with publishing approvals on Business at $19 per seat per month. Reply “intake” for a short walkthrough, or explore https://formkit.app.
plays.mechanic: Transplant assisted software implementation into agency client intake: show one form built in chat, reviewed, then published. Hypothesis: the approval requirement attracts higher-value team purchases rather than low-value solo demos.
plays.assetUsed: Formkit’s Claude/ChatGPT form-building workflow paired with Business publishing approvals—a specific intake-and-approval demonstration, not a generic AI pitch.
funnel: Forecast input: 1,000 distinct agency contacts reached during 90 days; assumption, grade D, conditional on mailbox health and test graduation.
Contacted → replied: 1% / 2% / 3% [supplied ClimbOS outreach benchmark, grade B].
Replied → booked walkthrough: 20% / 30% / 40% [supplied ClimbOS outreach benchmark, grade B].
Booked → attended: 60% / 80% / 90%; assumption, grade D.
Attended → first payment: 25% / 50% / 65%; assumption, grade D.
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether small agencies value publishing approvals enough to buy Business; the economics scenario assumes three monthly Business seats, not an observed seat mix.
plays.test: Assumed test: 500 distinct agency contacts, capped at $120 including owner time and credits; seek about 10 replies. Read the first approximately 200 contacts on day 21, finish the cohort by day 45, and check payments by day 60.
plays.killIf: Three or fewer replies from 500 contacts, or no payment after 10 attended walkthroughs. Stop instead of broadening to cheaper solo accounts.
plays.scaleIf: At day 21, at least four replies from 200 contacts and one paying agency permit 100 new agency contacts weekly. Continue only while actual CAC stays below half verified 12-month gross profit; the 90-day scenario uses 1,000 contacts and implies about 2.4 paying agencies.
plays.firstActionToday: Approve the small-agency target profile and record a two-minute intake-and-approval demonstration using dummy client details.
plays.climbosCanDo: Research targets, personalize first lines, send from the owner’s mailbox, manage one follow-up and stop on reply. After ramp-up, run 100 new agency contacts weekly, with booking and attribution handled in Pipeline.

plays.name: The chat-to-client walkthrough
plays.oneLiner: Make assistant integration useful enough for an educator to demonstrate—not merely mention.
plays.audience: Freelancer and agency workflow educators; start with https://www.beingfreelance.com/, https://theagencyoperator.ai/, https://growyouragency.group/ and https://community.bureauofdigital.com/newsletter-signup, then find smaller relevant creators.
plays.trigger: An educator needs a practical assistant workflow: turn a chat-built form into a branded client-intake process with a clear paid next step.
plays.hook: Would a client-intake walkthrough help your audience? Formkit lets you build and publish forms from Claude or ChatGPT. The free tier has unlimited forms, responses and members; Pro adds your own domain and Stripe payments at $6 per seat per month. Explore https://formkit.app. If it fits, would you show your own workflow? No praise or positive review requested.
plays.mechanic: Borrow an educator’s audience through an honest hands-on tutorial, then reuse that demonstration for a separate assistant-intent Google test. Hypothesis: this workflow attracts users who publish a useful form and subsequently need Pro.
plays.assetUsed: One real Claude/ChatGPT-to-client-intake demonstration, the unlimited free starting point, and a concrete Pro upgrade for domain or payment needs.
funnel: Editorial input: 100 distinct educator pitches during 90 days; assumption, grade D.
Pitched → replied: 10% / 15% / 20% [supplied ClimbOS creator-outreach benchmark, grade C].
Replied → agreed to demonstrate: 10% / 25% / 40%; assumption, grade D.
Agreed → published within the acquisition window: 40% / 70% / 90%; assumption, grade D.
Published demonstration → tracked visits per demonstration: 50 / 150 / 300; assumption, grade D, not claimed audience sizes.
Tracked visit → signup: 5% / 12% / 20%; assumption, grade D.
Signup → first published form: 40% / 60% / 80%; assumption, grade D.
First publication → first payment: 10% / 25% / 35%; assumption, grade D. Editorial P50 is approximately 7.1 paying workspaces.
Separate Google input: $55 media spend; CPC $2 / $1.10 / $0.75, equivalent to approximately 28 / 50 / 73 clicks; assumption, grade D.

Google click → signup: 10% / 20% / 30%; signup → first publication: 40% / 60% / 80%; first publication → first payment: 10% / 20% / 30%; each rate is an assumption, grade D. Google-test P50 is 1.2 paying workspaces; additional ad scaling is excluded.
plays.biggestUnknown: Whether educators publish without fees and send buyers rather than curious free users; no partnership is verified, and material collaborations require disclosure.
plays.test: Assumed initial cap: $120 total—$35 for 50 editorial pitches and $85 for the Google test, including $55 media spend and $30 setup/time/credits. Read replies and signups on day 21; check publications and payments by day 45.
plays.killIf: Three or fewer replies from 50 pitches, or no published demonstration by day 45, stops editorial expansion. Zero payments from 50 Google clicks by day 45 stops paid expansion.
plays.scaleIf: Editorial: at least eight replies from 50 pitches and one attributed payment permit completing 100 pitches. Google: at least three payments from 50 clicks permit incremental spending, capped at $600/month; both routes must maintain actual CAC below half verified 12-month gross profit.
plays.firstActionToday: Record a 90-second assistant-built intake demonstration and approve the first five educator targets; make no partnership claims.
plays.climbosCanDo: Research and pitch 10 educators weekly, prepare tracked walkthrough assets and draft Google ads for owner launch. Also check assistant-directory eligibility without forecasting approval or traffic: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12515353-build-with-the-apps-sdk and https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/11697096-anthropic-mcp-directory-policy.

output.portfolioNote: Proposed goal, assumption, grade D: 10 first-time paying workspaces by January 16, 2027. Acquisition P50 is 10.7; adding 2.25 upgrades from an unverified 500-workspace existing cohort gives 12.95, approximately 13, with no double-counting. These aggregate forecasts are assumptions, grade D. No supplied evidence supports a predictability-4 bankable play; the lifecycle card is a capped qualification experiment, not falsely labeled bankable. The two acquisition plays score 3 for predictability and 4 for distinctiveness; scores are editorial, ordered fit, predictability, reach per owner-hour, time to signal, compounding, cost, safety, distinctiveness. Planning assumptions, grade D: two owner hours weekly, $50/hour, monthly billing, 12 paid months and 80% gross margin imply $57.60 annual gross profit for one Pro seat or $547.20 for three Business seats. At those assumptions, 90-day all-in spending ceilings of $60 lifecycle, $500 agencies and $230 walkthroughs imply CAC of about $27, $208 and $28 respectively; these are ceilings, not verified costs. Before launch, approve actual credit charges and available hours; before scale, verify margin, billing, retention and seat mix, and require CAC below half actual 12-month gross profit. Advertising alone remains within $600/month; credits and owner time are separate costs. One mailbox handles both outbound plays: after ramp-up, 100 agency contacts plus 10 educator pitches weekly, with at most one follow-up each, stays within 50 total sends per working day. All test volumes, caps and decision thresholds are planning choices, not benchmarks.

reasons: B is the more coherent handoff: two active plays, identifiable audiences, concrete tests and a mostly consistent approval process. A reads like several revisions merged without reconciliation.

A contradicts itself on the paying-customer target, spending ceilings, whether advertising runs, whether educators replace or accompany agency outreach, and whether scaling requires three-month payback or half of annual gross profit. Those conflicts prevent an owner from knowing which instructions govern.

B keeps the proposed acquisition mechanics specific to Formkit: studio intake workflows and a focused Google Forms comparison. Its forecasts are generally presented as conditional rather than promised results.

B still has a serious economic weakness: its Search midpoint spends $1,800 for 0.81 customers—about $2,222 in advertising per customer before other costs. That is a poor starting proposition for this pricing and audience. A recognizes the low-price acquisition problem better, but its contradictory execution plan outweighs that advantage.
truthX: Repeatedly cites supposedly supplied ClimbOS benchmarks, service capabilities and credit arrangements that are not established in the provided material.
Claims a supplied MailerLite click benchmark, but provides only a homepage link rather than an identifiable supporting source.
Presents precise percentile forecasts without a stated statistical basis, and introduces an unexplained January 2027 deadline.
truthY: Attributes reply rates, booking rates, mailbox capacity and service capabilities to a supplied ClimbOS brief that is not present in the provided material.
Presents an agency-page URL and its existing templates as verified assets, although that specific page was not established by the supplied evidence.
Labels the Search play “bankable” despite explicitly unknown demand, CPC and paid conversion. Its percentile forecasts have no stated statistical basis.

basic.topIssue: The plan prioritizes acquisition tactics whose own forecasts imply unaffordable costs for a $6-per-seat product, without establishing larger account values or a concrete free-to-paid conversion mechanism.

expert.topIssue: The strategy contains conflicting targets, budgets, active channels and CAC rules across sections, leaving the owner without one executable 90-day plan.
